hook.line: Mariana needs to say when and where things happened, and *there was a protest* is not how a news story says it. Spanish gives events their own verb: they "have place".

examples.es: La reunión tuvo lugar el martes.
examples.en: The meeting took place on Tuesday.

examples.es: La manifestación tuvo lugar en la Plaza de Bolívar.
examples.en: The protest took place in Bolívar Square.
When will the meeting take place?

examples.es: Las protestas tuvieron lugar en varias ciudades.
examples.en: The protests took place in several cities.

examples.es: Las elecciones se celebraron el domingo.
examples.en: The elections were held on Sunday.

examples.es: El concierto se realizó en el parque.
examples.en: The concert was held in the park.

rule:
To say an event happened somewhere or at some time, use *tener lugar*: *tuvo lugar*, *tendrá lugar*. Only the verb changes, and it matches the event: *la protesta tuvo lugar*, *las protestas tuvieron lugar*. *Lugar* stays as it is.

Two more options for planned events: *se realizó* (was carried out) and *se celebró* (was held). They also agree with the event: *se celebraron las elecciones*.

In conversation people often just say *la reunión fue el martes*. *Tener lugar* is the version you read in the news and write in reports.
smallPrint: Teachers call *se realizó* and *se celebró* the passive with *se*. *Tener lugar* is a fixed expression: only *tener* changes.

yourTurn.why: Several protests, so the verb is plural: *tuvieron*.

pitfalls.wrong: La reunión tuvo un lugar el martes.
pitfalls.right: La reunión tuvo lugar el martes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. No *un* in this expression: *lugar* stays bare.

pitfalls.wrong: La reunión tomó lugar el martes.
pitfalls.right: La reunión tuvo lugar el martes.
pitfalls.why: English says "took place", but Spanish says "had place": *tener lugar*.

pitfalls.wrong: Las protestas tuvo lugar en varias ciudades.
pitfalls.right: Las protestas tuvieron lugar en varias ciudades.
pitfalls.why: The verb matches the event, and there is more than one.

pitfalls.wrong: El incendio se celebró en la noche.
pitfalls.right: El incendio tuvo lugar en la noche.
pitfalls.why: *Celebrarse* is only for planned events. A fire just *tiene lugar*.

personal: Think of an event from this week, like a meeting, a class or a game. Say when it took place, starting with *tuvo lugar* or *tuvieron lugar*.
